notes: PILOT BASE (args overlay for configs/workflow.json; research: docs/research/distribution-modeling/ performance-pilots synthesis). A quick, single-ticker run of the 7-step study that every other pilot-*.json stacks on: python -m dskit.pipeline workflow configs/workflow.json --args configs/pilot-base.json [--args configs/pilot-<x>.json]. QQQ only at the manifest's 7-day horizon, forward selection capped at 2 rounds and 300 bootstrap replicates, so one run takes minutes rather than the full study's quarter hour. It also adds four cheap challenger references that every pilot then reports on the same folds: standardized_empirical (the filtered-historical-simulation benchmark the study never ran: the empirical shape of the STANDARDIZED target r/a, whereas horizon_empirical is the empirical shape of RAW returns), two regime forests (quantile forests on seven volatility inputs; min_child 100 leaves at most a handful of vol/term-structure regimes per 450-date window, min_child 30 a finer split) and a small-input mixture MLP on the same seven inputs (a low-variance learner on the HAR-plus-implied-vol information set). standardized_empirical takes is_QQQ as its reference divisor: in a one-ticker lane that flag column is 1 on every row, so the model learns quantiles of the standardized target directly. That trick is valid ONLY for a single-lane run; a pooled or multi-ticker study needs a real seam (proposed in the research note). Read results in {work_dir}/report/report_QQQ/sections/comparisons.csv (skill of every model against every comparison reference, paired block bootstrap) and the step 6/7 study folders. Pilots screen, they never accept: rerun a winner on the full manifest before believing it.

standardized_empirical.notes: Filtered historical simulation: quantiles of y = r / reference_scale (trailing 22-session realized vol over the planned sessions), so the forecast scales with today's vol. horizon_empirical instead learns raw-return quantiles and divides by the row's scale, i.e. it ignores vol. The literature's standard benchmark (McNeil and Frey 2000; Kuester et al. 2006). If this beats horizon_empirical, the acceptance baseline is too weak and every earlier skill number is measured against the wrong bar.

regime_forest_coarse.notes: Regime segmentation without code: leaves of at least 100 rows split a 450-date window into a few volatility / term-structure / variance-premium regimes, each with its own empirical standardized distribution. Needs the quantile-forest extra (pip install -e '.[quantile-forest]' at the repo root). Earlier forests lost (-3.6% on 42 features, -13.5% on 198); this one tests the opposite end: few, economically motivated inputs and very coarse leaves.

regime_forest_fine.notes: The same seven inputs with leaves of 30 rows: more regimes, noisier shapes. Coarse beating fine says segmentation helps only when each segment keeps enough data.

small_input_mlp.notes: One Gaussian component, 8 hidden units, strong weight decay, three seeds averaged: the lowest-variance neural learner on the HAR-plus-implied-vol inputs (Christensen et al. 2023; Busch et al. 2011). Patience stops on the fold's calibration slice; epochs is only a ceiling (the study raises if patience is not exhausted before it, so it is set high). Set device to cpu on a machine without CUDA.
